title: Hours Well Spent
tagline: Spend Time Together. Build Skills. Make Memories.
description:
Hours Well Spent adds shared-time vignettes for SkyrimNet: short off-screen scenes where you and an NPC spend meaningful time together, then read how it went.

SkyrimNet characters sometimes want to do things that don’t neatly fit Skyrim’s mechanics — study, patrol, review ledgers, train, socialize, or simply spend an evening together. Instead of ignoring those moments or physically acting out every minute, Hours Well Spent lets you confirm the activity, fade to black, advance time, and receive a narrated result written from the characters involved, their memories, and the place they’re in.

Walk the battlements with Lydia. Study spells with Serana. Serve drinks with Saadia. Spar in the yard, review estate reports, or stay up too late over wine.

These scenes last from 1 to 9 hours, are remembered by everyone involved, and can grant light skill practice where it makes sense.

Inspired by SevActions’ off-screen events and Pass the Time.
author: whyregister
changelog:
New: the Plan the Hours lesser power. Plan the hours yourself: what (type anything or pick an idea), how long, who comes along (followers and people nearby, or nobody), and an optional Focus skill. Needs Magelight UI.
New: Change the plan on an NPC's proposal opens the planner filled in with their idea. Change the activity, hours or company, or add a Focus; quick accept works as before.
New: hours spent alone. The account is remembered, without anyone being told.
Fix: on some load orders the proposal fell back to message boxes even with Magelight UI installed ("Magelight has no prompt view" in the Papyrus log). The page has a name of its own now.
Fix: if Magelight wasn't ready when the game loaded, the page is set up again at the next proposal.
Fix: an account the model wrapped in a code fence was lost to the plain one-line account.
When the page can't be used, the Papyrus log says why.
Update by replacing 0.2.0. Safe mid-playthrough; the power is added on the next load.
